PFAS Removal Water Treatment Plant Project Statistics: • In the 2022 session, the legislature passed and the governor signed into law a requirement that on or before July 1, 2023, all public water supply systems in the state shall conduct monitoring for the presence of PFAS contaminants in drinking water supplied by the system. If the PFAS contaminants exceed the level of twenty parts per trillion (20 ppt), corrective action was required to be taken to reduce the levels to below this threshold. • $ 20,000,000 –State Fiscal Recovery Funds (ARPA) with conversion to RICAP being considered in 2024 legislative session • Status: Underway • Start 2022 • Completion 2026 Kingston Campus -Locus Map Not Actual Proposed Facilities For Illustration Purposes Only Ongoing Approved Project

Storm Water Management Project Statistics: • This project will include stormwater improvements to the existing drainage systems on campus. The water flow and storage capacity of the existing retention areas, drainage channels and pipes are frequently exceeded during major storm events and result in erosion and flooding to the downstream landscapes and buildings. The drainage improvements projects would provide additional storage volume and improve channel/pipe sizes and alignments to reduce the frequency of overtopping/flooding. • $ 4,700,000 -RICAP • Status: Design funding approved • Start 2023 • Complete 2026 Former Flooding at West Alumni Ave Former Flooding at Fraternity Circle Rain Garden @ CBLS Structures at West Alumni AveURI Subwatershed Ongoing Approved Project

Fraternity Circle Improvements -Phase 2 Project Statistics: • Phase 2 of this project will focus on Site Amenities and Pedestrian Networks. The project will create a new exterior environment which enhances the communal aspect of Greek life and gives Fraternity Circle a distinctive identity as part of URI. The work will include new pedestrian walkways, new site lighting and recreational amenities. • $1,400,000 -Third Party Funds • Status: Pending Funding Approval • Start 2025 • Complete 2026 Kingston Campus -Locus Map Ongoing Approved Project Fraternity Circle Master Plan

Utility Infrastructure -Phase 3 Project Statistics: • This is the third of three phases of work on the University’s primary utility systems. This project involves the engineering and construction of upgrades and component replacements to five municipal-level Kingston Campus utility systems. These systems include: • Steam/Condensate Distribution System • Water Distribution System • Electrical Distribution System • Sanitary Sewer System • Storm Water Management System • $ 9,191,250 -Expected RIHEBC Bonds • Status: Pending Funding Approval • Start 2024 • Complete 2027 Utilities Overview FY25 Request

Repaving & Hardscape Improvements Project Statistics: • The project involves the fifth phase of the University's progressive work to repave and reconstruct major parking facilities, internal roadways, and walkways across three of its four Campuses. In addition, the project includes improvements of important landscape elements that provide better exterior environments on campus. • $ 20,000,000 -Expected RIHEBC Bonds • Status: Pending Funding Approval • Start 2026 • Complete 2029 Kingston Campus Transportation Master Plan FY27 Request

Project Statistics: • This project would replace the east grandstands at Meade Field. It would provide modern grandstands including press box, 5,240 seats (6,596 total capacity with west stands), restrooms, concessions, field level training and taping room, equipment storage and full ADA compliance. • $42,800,000 -RICAP • Status: Design Phase Kicked off in March 2024 • Start 2023 • Complete 2027 Kingston Campus -Locus Map Meade East Grandstand Replacement Ongoing Approved Project

Project Statistics: • This maintains the track in the same general footprint reducing the costs and the need to displace any other fields or amenities within the existing athletic complex. This concept keeps the track in a north/south orientation but proposes to switch the common finish line to the northeast corner, which would allow athletes to finish most events with the prevailing winds at their backs. In the event winds change during a meet, the opposite finish line could be utilized based on the proposed layout. This concept proposes to remove several existing older buildings and a maintenance storage area close to the complex entrance off the northeast corner of the track. The removal of these buildings will ultimately create space for an ADA parking lot and a cleaner and more visually appealing entrance to the site. • $ 12,200,000 -RICAP • Status: Design Phase Kicked off in March 2024 • Start 2023 • Complete 2026 Kingston Campus -Locus Map Track & Field Replacement Ongoing Approved Project

Project Statistics: • In 2020 the University completed an advanced planning study for the replacement of the Tootell pools with a new natatorium building. Inclusive of converting the existing pools into an indoor playing field, this project had an expected price tag of $107MM assuming a 2027 completion. Rather than invest this level of funding, it was requested that a way was found to keep the pools in service for the next 6-8 years to allow time for a strategy for funding to be implemented. This project would provide that stop gap measure by funding critical repairs of the pool complex. • $ 6,200,000 -RICAP • Status: Design and Construction Underway • Start 2023 • Complete 2027 Kingston Campus -Locus Map Tootell Pool Repairs Ongoing Approved Project
